data.title: Maha FDA suspends Amazon, BigBasket Pune dark stores over safety violations
data.description:
The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Saturday suspended the food licences of Amazon and BigBasket dark stores located on Sinhagad Road in Pune city after finding "serious violations" of food safety and hygiene norms, officials said.

The action was taken under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, after officials found expired food products, unhygienic conditions and violations of Schedule IV provisions at both establishments during their inspections, they said.

Dark stores are retail or warehouse-like facilities designed exclusively for fulfilling online orders. They are neighbourhood micro-fulfilment centres closed to walk-in shoppers that store high-demand items to power ultra-fast online deliveries.

 

During an inspection at the Amazon dark store operated by Gajanan Inventories, officials found expired laddoos, pedhas and other food products. They also observed fungus growing on expired products, and dust in food containers. A ghee container had a broken lid and oil was leaking from the cartons, officials said.

Improper pest control measures and a lack of records related to personnel hygiene and sanitation were also found. Food and non-food items, including soap and ghee containers, were found stored together, they said.

At the BigBasket dark store operated by Innovative Retail Concept, officials found expired cakes, bread, milk rusk and chutney, and observed other food safety violations.

Food products were found lying on the floor.

The inspection also found a broken floor, an unhygienic cold room, leaking oil packets and improper pest control measures. Food and non-food items were found stored together, the officials said.

The action was carried out by Food Safety Officer Supriya Jagtap under the guidance of Assistant Commissioner (Food) Narayan Sarkate and the leadership of Joint Commissioner (Food) Shrikant Karkale.

Karkale said the FDA would take strict action against establishments found compromising consumer health and violating food safety regulations. He warned food businesses, including hotels, to strictly follow licence conditions, hygiene standards and food storage norms, failing which their licences could be suspended or cancelled.

data.title: India not rogue state: Wangchuk says police lifted curbs after court order
data.description:
Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk on Saturday joined the Leh Apex Body (LAB)-led protest in Leh, alleging that he had been kept under effective house arrest since November 11 and that police withdrew the security deployment outside his residence only after the matter came up before the court.

Addressing a press conference with LAB chairman Chering Dorje Lakruk at the protest site, Wangchuk questioned the legality of the restrictions imposed on his movement and accused the administration of using police personnel to carry out unjustified actions.

He also appealed to President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi to intervene, asserting that constitutional values and democratic freedoms must be upheld.

 

"India is not a rogue state. It is the world's largest democracy, and it has certain constitutional values and standards that must be upheld," he said.

Police on Friday night withdrew arrangements made to ensure compliance with a prohibitory order imposed against Wangchuk in Leh and said Wangchuk had not been placed under house arrest.

Recounting the events of November 11, Wangchuk said he was forcibly picked up while preparations were underway for the indefinite protest to press for resumption of dialogue with the centre and seek deferment of Hill Council polls scheduled for December 4.

"Those who came were wearing masks and hoodies, with their faces concealed. I would hesitate to even call them policemen because they looked more like goons," he said, alleging that although he had agreed to go to jail, he was instead taken to his residence in HIAL, where nearly two dozen local police and CRPF personnel, dressed in commando fatigues and carrying firearms, were deployed.

Wangchuk said he subsequently decided to challenge the restrictions through legal channels with the assistance of lawyers in Delhi and Ladakh.

He said an appeal was filed before the High Court bench in Leh on November 17 and listed for hearing the following day. He claimed that no government representative appeared during the November 18 hearing, following which the court gave the government time until November 19 to submit its response.

The activist stated that Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta appeared before the court on November 19 and sought time until November 23, which was granted.

"Taking advantage of this time, the authorities withdrew all the personnel deployed outside my residence Friday night," Wangchuk said.

In a post on X, Leh district police said, "Police arrangements which (were) placed to ensure compliance with prohibitory order have been withdrawn. ADM (Additional District magistrate), Leh has passed a prohibitory order against Wangchuk. It is clarified that he was not put under any house arrest as has been claimed." Wangchuk described the police statement as bizarre and questioned how the administration could deny restricting his movement when he had allegedly been prevented from stepping outside his residence.

Wangchuk alleged that the administration was effectively denying restrictions when faced with judicial scrutiny.

"This is an extremely strange way for a government to function. The State is behaving like a rogue state, where anyone can simply be picked up and detained. But when it is required to face the truth in a court of law, it suddenly claims that nothing happened and that there was no such detention," he said, referring to his earlier arrest under NSA.

Wangchuk, however, expressed sympathy for the police personnel and officers deployed outside his residence, alleging that they were being made to carry out actions that could compromise their professional responsibilities.

"I hope that when they joined the civil services, whether the IPS or IAS, they did so with great aspirations and a genuine desire to serve the country. Today, however, they are being used and misused like pawns in what resembles a mafia gang," he said.

Appealing to people across the country, Wangchuk said such practices must stop, asserting that India, as the world's largest democracy, must uphold constitutional values and ensure that police officers and government officials are not used for unlawful actions.

"I have appealed to President Murmu and the prime minister to put an end to this lawlessness and ensure that our officers and police personnel are allowed to discharge their duties with dignity and within the bounds of the law," he said.

Wangchuk also defended the ongoing sit-in protest, saying he had joined his colleagues at the protest site and that the demonstration, which had continued for 10 days, was peaceful and authorised.

Turning to the upcoming LAHDC elections, he renewed his appeal to the government not to hold the polls during winter, arguing that a substantial section of the population would be outside Ladakh and unable to participate.

"On the one hand, we send a message to the world that we take democracy to the last citizen, even flying helicopters to polling stations where there are just two voters. On the other hand, we are excluding 40 to 50 per cent of the population and conducting elections during winter, amid snowfall, while also subjecting government officials to immense hardship," he said.

Wangchuk maintained that people were not opposed to elections but wanted them conducted during a season conducive to public participation and the smooth deployment of officials, particularly in remote and snowbound areas.

He said the government should reconsider its approach and ensure that democratic processes in Ladakh were inclusive rather than imposed on the people.

data.title: NGT takes suo motu cognisance of illegal mining near MP's Bajranggarh Fort
data.description:
The National Green Tribunal (NGT) has taken suo motu (on its own) cognisance of alleged illegal mining and frequent blasting in the hills adjoining the historic Bajranggarh Fort in Madhya Pradesh's Guna district and issued notices to five authorities.

The tribunal impleaded the Madhya Pradesh government through the Guna district magistrate, the Member Secretary of the Madhya Pradesh Pollution Control Board, Guna Municipal Council, the Divisional Forest Officer, Guna, and the District Mining Officer, Guna, as respondents. They have been asked to reply ahead of the next hearing on December 23, an official said.

The NGT's Bhopal-based Central Zonal Bench, comprising Chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava and expert member Sudhir Kumar Chaturvedi, registered an original application based on a news report in a Hindi newspaper on November 17 on mining and stone quarrying in the hills near the 16th-17th century Bajranggarh fort.

 

The NGT observed that the matter appeared to involve violations of environmental norms, which could attract provisions of the Environment (Protection) Act, the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, and the Environment Impact Assessment Notification.

The bench also referred to the Supreme Court's 2021 judgement in the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai versus Ankita Sinha case, which recognised the NGT's power to take up matters suo motu.

According to the newspaper report, nine mining leases have been allotted in the area over the past decade, though excavation was being carried out at several locations over areas many times larger than those approved under the mining leases.

The report further stated that crusher machines were continuously breaking stones on the hills adjoining the fort, near the Aron-Sironj State Highway, and regular blasting was being carried out to break rocks. These were causing nearby houses and even the fort walls to tremble.

The report also flagged the absence of wire fencing and warning signs around deep mining pits, alleging that inadequate safety measures posed a serious risk of accidents.

It raised questions over the monitoring and oversight of the Mineral Department and the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

data.title: India to host WorldSkills Asia 2027 in Greater Noida, announces PM Modi
data.description:
India will host the WorldSkills Asia competition in Greater Noida in Uttar Pradesh in 2027, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced on Saturday, saying the country was moving towards becoming the world's skill capital.

The 48th WorldSkills Competition was held in Shanghai, China, in September 2026. The competition is the world's largest international gathering of skills talent.

Addressing the fifth National Skill Convocation here, Modi said the international competition would bring young participants from several Asian countries to Uttar Pradesh.

"Next year, in 2027, India will host the WorldSkills Asia competition. Young people from across Asia will come here, and this event will be organised in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh," he said.

 

Congratulating Uttar Pradesh in advance for hosting the international event, Modi said the country was progressing towards becoming the world's skill capital.

"India is moving forward towards becoming the skill capital of the world. And at the centre of this ambition are you," he told the young participants, referring to the country's skilled workforce.

Modi said he was speaking not just about India's aspirations but also its potential to contribute to the global skilled workforce.

Union defence minister Rajnath Singh, Minister for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Jayant Chaudhary, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, and UP BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary were also present at the event, among others.

data.title: ITI graduates deserve same respect as IIT alumni, says PM Narendra Modi
data.description:
Underlining the imperative of skilling in an AI-driven world, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday asserted that he was striving to accord the same respect to Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) as to the premier Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs).
 
Addressing the '5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh' in Lucknow on Saturday evening, Modi said that while only a handful possessed "paper certificates" (purporting to high-value degrees), big corporations were functioning owing to a workforce of 200-300 ITI pass-outs.
 
"Today, doomsayers are talking about job losses due to AI, but no one can take away the jobs of those having skills," he predicted.
 
Lamenting that the parents of ITI students felt embarrassed by the ITI tag, the PM said he was determined to alter the status quo in favour of the skilling ecosystem.
 
 
He waxed eloquent on the traditional craftsmanship of India, including chikankari of Lucknow, pashmina of Kashmir, Kanjeevaram of Tamil Nadu, etc., saying the ancient Indian societal fabric centred around skills.
 
Modi noted that the invaders' first assault was on our skills, while the education system later introduced by the British under Macaulay was focused on churning out clerks.
 
"As a result, we started focussing on clerical jobs, and the skills took a back-seat due to our slavery mindset," the PM underlined.
 
Further, Modi claimed that the trade deals India was inking with foreign countries encompassed a high demand for Indian skilled workers in such offshore geographies.
 
"These countries do not require people with university degrees but ITI workers possessing skills," Modi added.
 
He said the Gulf countries also acknowledged that their sparkling cities and flagship projects were possible only due to Indian skilled workers and not their wealth.
 
Modi recalled that in 2023, he had nudged people to invest in PSUs, while last year he had urged people to defer gold purchases.
 
He claimed both his statements had proved true to the benefit of people.
 
"Today, I am making another statement. More than the suited-booted, carrying paper certificates, those people with skills will command greater respect, and they will be in high demand," he asserted.
 
The PM opined that the dream of Viksit Bharat in another 20 years would be based on skills. "Earlier, India imported mobile phones, today Made in India mobile phones are exported globally."
 
Since 2014, more than 5,000 new ITIs have been set up, while an additional 0.5 million students have been enrolled, even as 30 new trades are being taught, he claimed.
 
These include aeronautical, cyber security, drone and green hydrogen, semiconductor technicians, etc.
 
He said 500 million people had come out of poverty in India, which was a big achievement and one that would pave the path to becoming a developed nation.
 
Talking about the Gulf crisis, he said plumbers were in short supply in India for piped natural gas (PNG) connections.
 
"India is progressing to becoming the skills capital of the world owing to you people (ITI students)," Modi said.
 
Next year, India will host the World Skills Competition in Greater Noida.
 
Modi's remarks came against the backdrop of his recently questioning India Inc for not raising employee salaries or expanding its workforce despite receiving tax relief and benefiting from an improved business environment.
 
In 2014, the corporate tax rate was 30 per cent; we reduced it to 22 per cent. For income up to ₹12 lakh, there is no income tax.
 
"But your hunger is such that, no matter how much you are fed, your stomach is not full. Have you increased the salaries of your employees? Have you increased your number of employees?” Modi asked at a Ficci event in New Delhi.
 
Instituted in the 2021-22 academic session, the Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh has emerged as an annual national platform to recognise excellence in skill development and celebrate the transition of skilled youth from training to the world of work.
 
Since its inception, the platform has felicitated all-India toppers and high achievers from the skill development ecosystem, fostering a culture of pride, achievement and aspiration around vocational education and skilled careers.
 
This year, 52 national-level toppers from Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) and Institutes for Training of Trainers (IToTs) were felicitated for their outstanding achievements.

data.title: Shivakumar urges ASHA workers to end protest, promises permanent solution
data.description:
Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Saturday appealed to protesting ASHA workers to call off their agitation, assuring them that the government was considering a comprehensive and permanent solution to their demands.

In a post on X, Shivakumar said the government stood with the workers and would take appropriate steps after discussing their demands with the Cabinet.

Making an appeal on behalf of the government, he said he understood the difficulties and hardships they were facing while fighting for their demands.

"It pains me to see you fighting day and night, staying away from your families. You are not just ASHA workers to me; you are like my own sisters," he said.

 

The CM reiterated that the government was considering a comprehensive and permanent solution to their demands in the coming days.

"We stand with you and will discuss the matter with the Cabinet and take appropriate steps," he said.

"As an elder brother, I appeal to you to kindly respond to my request and call off your protest. We respect your service, hard work and sacrifices. The government is committed to addressing your demands and providing an appropriate solution," he added.

Despite repeated appeals from the government to withdraw their agitation, the Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) workers have continued their protest, maintaining that they would call it off only after the government issued a specific order addressing their demands.

The workers began an indefinite day-and-night protest at Freedom Park on Tuesday, demanding that the government fix their monthly honorarium at Rs 15,000 and address their other pending demands.

They have also reportedly raised concerns over the non-payment of honoraria for work related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the educational and social survey.

data.title: Congress youth wing takes protest against Meta to its India offices
data.description:
The youth wing of India's main opposition Congress party clashed with police outside Meta offices, protesting the company's removal of ​some Instagram accounts of its members, according to footage released by the group on ​Saturday.

Meta declined to comment on the protests, an escalation by the influential political group in the company's biggest market ‌by users. Debate is growing in India about potential risks to free speech from the increasingly strict efforts of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government to remove social media content it objects to.

Modi's government says it orders content taken down only if it breaches local laws, can harm public safety or national security. Congress has long accused Meta and other social media platforms of curbing dissent online by removing party accounts, favouring Modi's government.

 

Meta has said it restricts content in India to comply with local laws.

MODI'S PARTY ACCUSES CONGRESS OF VANDALISM

Pradeep Bhandari, a national spokesperson for Modi's ruling party, criticised Congress' actions on Saturday, saying they had "not only vandalised and destroyed Meta's office in Hyderabad" but were also "flaunting it on social media".

"This is Congress Model: Vandalise offices of Private companies," he wrote.

India's IT ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

In ‌Hyderabad on Friday, protesters carrying placards chanted slogans as they stormed into the building that houses Meta's offices, smashing plants to the ground and clashing with police, according to footage released by the Indian Youth Congress' X account.

Another video showed Congress workers spray-painting anti-Meta slogans on walls outside the building that houses its Mumbai office, clashing with security guards who tried to stop them. In Gurugram near New Delhi, Congress workers chanted slogans and held banners reading "restore youth Congress accounts", official online posts showed.

The Indian Youth Congress posted warnings on X that it would "storm your offices across the country and stage protests" unless Instagram accounts ​of its leaders are restored.

Two such accounts were restored after Friday's protests, but thousands of accounts of journalists, creators and influencers critical ‌of the government remain restricted, Manu Jain, who is in charge of social media for the youth group, told Reuters on Saturday.

Meta must explain how its algorithms restrict posts and must restore accounts taken down on government orders, he ​added.

Reporters Without Borders has ‌said the removal of journalistic content from social media has been on the rise in India this year, and free speech activists ‌say a new government rule gives social media companies hardly any time to review and decide on takedown requests.

In February, Modi's government ordered social media companies to take down unlawful content within three hours of being notified about it, tightening ‌an earlier ​36-hour timeline.

Meta disclosures ​show that it restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts in India under local laws in the first half of 2026, second only to Indonesia and up from about 70,000 in the whole of 2025.

"The ‌large majority of these items ​included instances where we were obligated to proactively restrict content ... based on local law requirements," Meta said.

data.title: India, Canada conclude sixth round of talks for proposed trade pact
data.description:
India and Canada have concluded the sixth round of negotiations for a trade agreement, aimed at unlocking new opportunities in trade and investment, and diversifying supply chains, an official statement said on Saturday.

The negotiations covered key areas, including trade in goods, trade in services, rules of origin, trade remedies, intellectual property and investment promotion, the commerce ministry said.

Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal held a meeting with Glenn Purves, Vice Minister of International Trade of Canada, and his delegation to review the progress of negotiations for the proposed Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).

The ten-day talks concluded on November 20.

"Both sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to concluding an ambitious, balanced and commercially meaningful agreement that delivers tangible benefits to farmers, industries, businesses and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in both countries," it said.

data.title: Karnataka seeks 50 more workdays under VB-G RAM G in view of drought
data.description:
Karnataka Minister Eshwar Khandre on Saturday said the state government has written to the Centre seeking an additional 50 days of work under the VB-G RAM G scheme, which would take the annual employment guarantee to 175 days per job card holder, in view of drought conditions.

The Centre has fixed the guarantee at 125 days a year for each rural job card holder under the scheme.

The state sought the extra days to help farmers and rural labourers affected by deficient rainfall, Khandre said.

The Rural Development and Panchayat Raj minister was speaking after visiting a desilting work site at a check dam within the Adavi Somapur Gram Panchayat limits in Gadag taluk, where he interacted with workers.

 

"Due to drought, rural people are forced to migrate in search of work. To prevent this, continuous employment must be provided under the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) scheme," he told the workers.

Keeping in view the interests of farmers who are facing difficulties due to deficient rainfall, we have written to the Centre requesting that another 50 days of work be added to the existing 125 days, taking the total to 175 days per job card," he said.

During the interaction, farmers urged the minister to provide an opportunity to take up trench-cum-bund works, which would benefit both farmers and agricultural labourers. Khandre responded positively to the request.

The minister advised workers to enrol under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) and Atal Pension Yojana (APY).

Khandre said gram panchayat officials were conducting surveys daily under the state government's Bhoo Guarantee scheme, which aims to provide digital property records, and urged residents to make use of the initiative.

He symbolically handed over digital property documents to two beneficiaries, according to a release from the minister's office.

data.title: COP31 climate talks extend into overtime amid deadlock on fossil fuels
data.description:
Work crews were boxing up the venue of this year's United Nations climate talks in Turkiye, as negotiators went into overtime on Saturday in an attempt to reach a final agreement to address global warming. But hopes are slim that additional discussions will result in concrete plans to drastically slash the use of fossil fuels.

The added day of talks came as the two-week annual summit, called COP31, which was supposed to end Friday, drew strong condemnation from activists and some countries for failing to mention fossil fuels in a draft of the final agreement. The final document is meant to address how the world will deal with climate change, which is contributing to devastating heat waves, floods and other disasters.

 

To avert the most catastrophic effects of warming, experts said the world needs to urgently and drastically cut emissions from the use of coal, oil and gas.

In the lead up to these talks, the UN announced that the world will likely blow past the 2015 Paris Agreement goal of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial temperatures.

"No one knows what is happening behind closed doors, or what the outcome of COP31 will be," said Teresa Anderson, global lead on climate justice at ActionAid International.

Climate talks go into overtime

Inside an area of the COP31 venue known as the "pavilions," where countries showcased their climate policies and hosted panel discussions, workers were packing up electronics and other belongings Saturday morning.

The hallways, normally bustling with participants, stood largely empty, with only a handful of security guards seen taking photos in front of the deserted pavilions.

"COP31 is in a bleak overtime, with dwindling food and water, and no sign of any progress since the alarmingly underwhelming texts we saw earlier," said Rachel Cleetus from the Union of Concerned Scientists, who is at the venue in the Mediterranean coastal city of Antalya.

Earlier during the summit, the nonprofit Climate Action Tracker warned that progress on slowing global warming has stalled for the past five years, even as disasters -- including this year's heat waves in Europe and flooding in Nepal -- become more deadly.

Countries most vulnerable to climate change, including small island nations whose lands are battered by rising seas, also say wealthy nations that caused the climate crisis must contribute more to UN funds to help them recover from disasters and adapt to a warmer world.

The United States, a major polluter and the world's largest economy, did not participate directly in this year's talks.

Next year's climate summit is scheduled to take place in Ethiopia's capital, Addis Ababa, in November 2027.

Criticism of COP31 grows

On Friday, a protester wearing a red noose around his neck and a vest emblazoned with the slogan "you are killing the future" interrupted official COP proceedings by clambering onto a table and shouting "You take out fossil fuels. You killed 1.5. There is no money. Just kill me now. The Global South cannot wait." The Global South is a term that isn't geographical, but a reference to developing countries in general.

"You keep doing nothing at all. Nothing at all. Kill me now. Kill me now," the protester shouted as he was escorted out of the room by security.

The demonstration interrupted Turkiye's Minister of Environment and COP31 co-president Murat Kurum, who said "let's try to maintain the peace in the room" before continuing with his scheduled remarks.

"Yesterday, of course, this place was buzzing and today it's nearly empty. But all the key negotiators are here, civil society is here watching the negotiations and waiting for the next iteration of the text," said Harjeet Singh, a strategic adviser to the Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative, who has attended 18 climate summits.

"We are still stuck with many, many disagreements and nobody knows how long this will go on," he said.
